name: ScrollFloat-TS-TW

frames.best_why: Title and caption are both settled and complete, with the scroll hint well out of the way.

tagline: Oversized characters stretch and drop into place on scroll.
summary: A huge word and a smaller caption assemble letter by letter as the block scrolls into view, each character dropping from below, stretched tall, then snapping to its final shape.
appearance: A very large black-weight white word holds the centre of a black stage, with a smaller muted grey caption beneath it. Characters are tightly tracked in a clean geometric sans.
behaviour: Scrolling brings each character up in turn from below, tall and faint, then snaps it to normal width and full opacity so the words settle into a line. Scrolling back lifts the letters away again.
demo_content: "StashUI" over "every character floats into place", with a SCROLL DOWN hint above.
search_phrases: letters float into place on scroll
big title animates as page scrolls
hero word stretches and drops in
smooth text entrance for landing page
use_when: A landing page manifesto or big brand headline should assemble as the reader scrolls.
avoid_when: Content above the fold: it only animates once the block scrolls into view.
customise: The text is passed as children; duration, easing, start and end scroll points, stagger and class names are props. Character splitting is fixed.
weight_why: A scroll timeline over one line of character spans; nothing renders per frame.

a11y.note: The copy is real text, but characters start invisible and there is no reduced-motion fallback.

issues: The caption is cut off at the bottom edge in frames 3 and 4.
polish_why: Strong scale and a springy settle; the giant word crowds a tight crop.
title: Scroll Float
